E.1 Technical Lemmata

Lemma E.5.

Let (𝐗,𝐘)∈ℝd×N×ℝK×N(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times N}\times\mathbb{R}^{K\times N} be a dataset where the labels 𝐘\mathbf{Y} are written in columns of one-hot vectors. For each pair (𝐱,𝐲)∈ℝD×ℝK(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})\in\mathbb{R}^{D}\times\mathbb{R}^{K}, and a weight 𝐖1∈ℝK×d\mathbf{W}_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times d}, define the cross-entropy as:

ℓ(𝐖1)=def.−∑k=1K𝐲klog(softmax(𝐖1𝐱))k=log(1+∑k≠yexp(𝐰k−𝐰y)⊤𝐱i)\ell(\mathbf{W}_{1})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mbox{def.}}}{{=}}-\sum_{k=1}^{K}\mathbf{y}_{k}\log\left(\text{softmax}(\mathbf{W}_{1}\mathbf{x})\right)_{k}=\log\left(1+\sum_{k\neq y}\exp(\mathbf{w}_{k}-\mathbf{w}_{y})^{\top}\mathbf{x}_{i}\right)

where y=arg​maxk∈[K]⁡[𝐲]ky=\argmax_{k\in[K]}[\mathbf{y}]_{k} is the class index of 𝐱\mathbf{x}. Let ℒ1​(𝐖1)=CE​(𝐖1​𝐗,𝐘)\mathcal{L}_{1}(\mathbf{W}_{1})=\text{CE}(\mathbf{W}_{1}\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y}) be the average cross-entropy loss of the dataset (𝐗,𝐘)(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y}). Then the loss gradient ∇ℒ1​(𝐖1)\nabla\mathcal{L}_{1}(\mathbf{W}_{1}) is

∇ℒ1​(𝐖1)=1N​(𝐒−𝐘)​𝐗⊤\nabla\mathcal{L}_{1}(\mathbf{W}_{1})=\frac{1}{N}(\mathbf{S}-\mathbf{Y})\mathbf{X}^{\top}

where 𝐒=(𝐬1,…​𝐬N)\mathbf{S}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{s}_{1},...\mathbf{s}_{N}\end{pmatrix} and 𝐬i=softmax​(𝐖1​𝐱i)\mathbf{s}_{i}=\text{softmax}(\mathbf{W}_{1}\mathbf{x}_{i}) for each ii. In particular, 𝟏K⊤∇ℒ1(𝐖1)=0\bm{1}_{K}^{\top}\nabla\mathcal{L}_{1}(\mathbf{W}_{1})=0.

Proof.

The expression of the loss gradient comes from simple calculus. The second statement comes from the fact that the L1 norms of a post-softmax vector and an one-hot vector are both equal to 1, that is,

𝟏K⊤​𝐬i=𝟏K⊤​𝐲i=1​∀i.\bm{1}_{K}^{\top}\mathbf{s}_{i}=\bm{1}_{K}^{\top}\mathbf{y}_{i}=1\,\forall i.

∎

Lemma E.6.

Assume the weight 𝐖t\mathbf{W}_{t} is updated as follows:

𝐕t+1=β​𝐕t+𝐆t+λ​𝐖t𝐖t+1=𝐖t−η​𝐕t+1,\displaystyle\begin{split}&\mathbf{V}_{t+1}=\beta\mathbf{V}_{t}+\mathbf{G}_{t}+\lambda\mathbf{W}_{t}\\ &\mathbf{W}_{t+1}=\mathbf{W}_{t}-\eta\mathbf{V}_{t+1},\end{split}

where 𝐆t\mathbf{G}_{t} depends on 𝐖t\mathbf{W}_{t}. Define

α=def.1K​‖𝐖t⊤​𝟏‖22≥0.\alpha\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mbox{def.}}}{{=}}\frac{1}{K}\|\mathbf{W}_{t}^{\top}\bm{1}\|_{2}^{2}\geq 0.

Then we have the expression:

1η​(αt+1−αt)=−2​β​ωt−2​γt−2​λ​αt+η​νt+1\frac{1}{\eta}(\alpha_{t+1}-\alpha_{t})=-2\beta\omega_{t}-2\gamma_{t}-2\lambda\alpha_{t}+\eta\nu_{t+1}

where ωt=def.⟨𝐕t​𝐖t⊤,𝐉^⟩\omega_{t}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mbox{def.}}}{{=}}\langle\mathbf{V}_{t}\mathbf{W}_{t}^{\top},\hat{\mathbf{J}}\rangle, γt=def.⟨𝐆t​𝐖t⊤,𝐉^⟩\gamma_{t}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mbox{def.}}}{{=}}\langle\mathbf{G}_{t}\mathbf{W}_{t}^{\top},\hat{\mathbf{J}}\rangle, νt=def.⟨𝐕t​𝐕t⊤,𝐉^⟩\nu_{t}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mbox{def.}}}{{=}}\langle\mathbf{V}_{t}\mathbf{V}_{t}^{\top},\hat{\mathbf{J}}\rangle.

Proof.

Let 𝐂t=def.𝐖t​𝐖t⊤\mathbf{C}_{t}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mbox{def.}}}{{=}}\mathbf{W}_{t}\mathbf{W}_{t}^{\top} be the covariance matrix. Notice that αt=⟨𝐂t,𝐉^⟩\alpha_{t}=\langle\mathbf{C}_{t},\hat{\mathbf{J}}\rangle where 𝐉^=1K​𝟏𝟏⊤\hat{\mathbf{J}}=\frac{1}{K}\bm{1}\bm{1}^{\top}. By update rule of 𝐖t\mathbf{W}_{t} and 𝐕t\mathbf{V}_{t}:

1η​(𝐂t+1−𝐂t)\displaystyle\frac{1}{\eta}(\mathbf{C}_{t+1}-\mathbf{C}_{t}) =1η​((𝐖t−η​𝐕t+1)​(𝐖t−η​𝐕t+1)⊤−𝐂t)\displaystyle=\frac{1}{\eta}\left((\mathbf{W}_{t}-\eta\mathbf{V}_{t+1})(\mathbf{W}_{t}-\eta\mathbf{V}_{t+1})^{\top}-\mathbf{C}_{t}\right)
=−(𝐕t+1​𝐖t⊤+𝐖t​𝐕t+1⊤)+η​𝐕t+1​𝐕t+1⊤.\displaystyle=-(\mathbf{V}_{t+1}\mathbf{W}_{t}^{\top}+\mathbf{W}_{t}\mathbf{V}_{t+1}^{\top})+\eta\mathbf{V}_{t+1}\mathbf{V}_{t+1}^{\top}.

Applying the dot product ⟨⋅,𝐉^⟩F\langle\cdot,\hat{\mathbf{J}}\rangle_{F} on both sides, and denote ωt=def.⟨𝐕t​𝐖t⊤,𝐉^⟩\omega_{t}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mbox{def.}}}{{=}}\langle\mathbf{V}_{t}\mathbf{W}_{t}^{\top},\hat{\mathbf{J}}\rangle, γt=def.⟨𝐆t​𝐖t⊤,𝐉^⟩\gamma_{t}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mbox{def.}}}{{=}}\langle\mathbf{G}_{t}\mathbf{W}_{t}^{\top},\hat{\mathbf{J}}\rangle, νt=def.⟨𝐕t​𝐕t⊤,𝐉^⟩\nu_{t}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mbox{def.}}}{{=}}\langle\mathbf{V}_{t}\mathbf{V}_{t}^{\top},\hat{\mathbf{J}}\rangle, we have

1η​(αt+1−αt)\displaystyle\frac{1}{\eta}(\alpha_{t+1}-\alpha_{t}) =−2​⟨𝐕t+1​𝐖t⊤,𝐉^⟩+η⁡⟨𝐕t+1​𝐕t+1⊤,𝐉^⟩\displaystyle=-2\langle\mathbf{V}_{t+1}\mathbf{W}_{t}^{\top},\hat{\mathbf{J}}\rangle+\eta\langle\mathbf{V}_{t+1}\mathbf{V}_{t+1}^{\top},\hat{\mathbf{J}}\rangle
=−2​⟨(β​𝐕t+𝐆t+λ​𝐖t)​𝐖t⊤,𝐉^⟩+η​νt+1\displaystyle=-2\langle(\beta\mathbf{V}_{t}+\mathbf{G}_{t}+\lambda\mathbf{W}_{t})\mathbf{W}_{t}^{\top},\hat{\mathbf{J}}\rangle+\eta\nu_{t+1}
=−2​β​ωt−2​γt−2​λ​αt+η​νt+1\displaystyle=-2\beta\omega_{t}-2\gamma_{t}-2\lambda\alpha_{t}+\eta\nu_{t+1} (22)

where in the first line we use the fact that 𝐉^\hat{\mathbf{J}} is symmetric.

∎

Lemma E.7.

Assume λ,β∈(0,1)\lambda,\beta\in(0,1) such that 2​λlog⁡β−1<1\frac{2\lambda}{\log\beta^{-1}}<1. The solution of the following ODE:

α˙​(t)=−λ⁡(∫0tβt−τ​α​(τ)​𝑑τ)\dot{\alpha}(t)=-\lambda\left(\int_{0}^{t}\beta^{t-\tau}\alpha(\tau)d\tau\right) (23)

with initial condition α⁡(0)=α0>0\alpha(0)=\alpha_{0}>0 admits the following bound:

α⁡(t)≤C​α0​exp⁡(−λlog⁡β−1​t)\alpha(t)\leq C\alpha_{0}\exp\left(-\frac{\lambda}{\log\beta^{-1}}t\right)

for some absolute constant C>1C>1.

Proof.

Observe that we can write the integral in convolution:

∫0tβt−τ​α​(τ)​𝑑τ=(ϕ∗α)​(t),whereϕ⁡(t)=βt.\int_{0}^{t}\beta^{t-\tau}\alpha(\tau)d\tau=\bigl(\phi*\alpha\bigr)(t),\quad\text{where}\quad\phi(t)=\beta^{t}.

Hence (23) can be written as

α˙​(t)=−λ⁡(ϕ∗α)​(t).\dot{\alpha}(t)=-\lambda\bigl(\phi*\alpha\bigr)(t).

Let ℒ​{ψ⁡(t)}​(s)=∫0∞e−s​t​ψ​(t)​𝑑t\mathcal{L}\{\psi(t)\}(s)=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\infty}e^{-st}\psi(t)dt denote the Laplace transform. Denote

𝒜⁡(s)=ℒ⁡{α⁡(t)}​(s),F⁡(s)=ℒ⁡{ϕ⁡(t)}​(s).\mathcal{A}(s)=\mathcal{L}\{\alpha(t)\}(s),\quad F(s)=\mathcal{L}\{\phi(t)\}(s).

Taking the Laplace transform of both sides:

ℒ⁡{α˙​(t)}​(s)=−λ​ℒ​{(ϕ∗α)​(t)}​(s).\mathcal{L}\{\dot{\alpha}(t)\}(s)=-\lambda\mathcal{L}\{(\phi*\alpha)(t)\}(s). (24)

And by integration by part and the property of convolution,

ℒ⁡{α˙​(t)}​(s)=s​𝒜​(s)−α⁡(0)andℒ⁡{(ϕ∗α)​(t)}​(s)=F⁡(s)​𝒜​(s).\mathcal{L}\{\dot{\alpha}(t)\}(s)=s\mathcal{A}(s)-\alpha(0)\quad\text{and}\quad\mathcal{L}\{(\phi*\alpha)(t)\}(s)=F(s)\mathcal{A}(s).

Hence

s​𝒜​(s)−α⁡(0)=−λ​F​(s)​𝒜​(s).s\mathcal{A}(s)-\alpha(0)=-\lambda F(s)\mathcal{A}(s).

Since βt=e(log⁡β)​t\beta^{t}=e^{(\log\beta)t}, we get

F⁡(s)=ℒ​{βt}​(s)=ℒ​{e(log⁡β)​t}​(s)=1s−log⁡(β) for ​s>log⁡(β).F(s)=\mathcal{L}\{\beta^{t}\}(s)=\mathcal{L}\!\bigl\{e^{(\log\beta)t}\bigr\}(s)=\frac{1}{s-\log(\beta)}\quad\text{ for }s>\log(\beta).

Substitute this back to Eq. (24) and we get:

s​𝒜​(s)−α⁡(0)\displaystyle s\mathcal{A}(s)-\alpha(0) =−λ​1s−log⁡(β)​𝒜​(s)\displaystyle=-\lambda\frac{1}{s-\log(\beta)}\mathcal{A}(s)
s​𝒜​(s)+λs−log⁡(β)​𝒜​(s)\displaystyle s\mathcal{A}(s)+\frac{\lambda}{s-\log(\beta)}\mathcal{A}(s) =α⁡(0)\displaystyle=\alpha(0)
𝒜⁡(s)​(s+λs−log⁡(β)⏟s2−s​log⁡(β)+λs−log⁡(β))\displaystyle\mathcal{A}(s)\Bigl(\underbrace{s+\frac{\lambda}{s-\log(\beta)}}_{\frac{s^{2}-s\log(\beta)+\lambda}{s-\log(\beta)}}\Bigr) =α⁡(0)\displaystyle=\alpha(0)
𝒜⁡(s)\displaystyle\mathcal{A}(s) =α⁡(0)⋅[s−log⁡(β)]s2−s​log⁡(β)+λ⏟(s−r1)​(s−r2)\displaystyle=\alpha(0)\cdot\frac{\bigl[s-\log(\beta)\bigr]}{\underbrace{s^{2}-s\log(\beta)+\lambda}_{(s-r_{1})(s-r_{2})}}

where r1,r2=log⁡(β)±[log⁡(β)]2−4​λ2.r_{1},r_{2}=\frac{\log(\beta)\pm\sqrt{\bigl[\log(\beta)\bigr]^{2}-4\lambda}}{2}. We do partial fractions and matching coefficients gives:

s−log⁡(β)(s−r1)​(s−r2)=As−r1+Bs−r2⟹A+B=1,−log⁡(β)=−A​r2−B​r1.\frac{s-\log(\beta)}{(s-r_{1})(s-r_{2})}=\frac{A}{s-r_{1}}+\frac{B}{s-r_{2}}\implies A+B=1,\quad-\log(\beta)=-Ar_{2}-Br_{1}.

Since r1+r2=log⁡(β)r_{1}+r_{2}=\log(\beta), one finds

A=r2r2−r1,B=−r1r2−r1.A=\frac{r_{2}}{r_{2}-r_{1}},\quad B=-\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}-r_{1}}.

Thus

𝒜⁡(s)=α⁡(0)​[r2r2−r1​1s−r1−r1r2−r1​1s−r2].\mathcal{A}(s)=\alpha(0)\left[\frac{r_{2}}{r_{2}-r_{1}}\frac{1}{s-r_{1}}-\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}-r_{1}}\frac{1}{s-r_{2}}\right].

Recall the inverse of Laplacian transform: ℒ−1​{1s−r}​(t)=er​t.\mathcal{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-r}\}(t)=e^{rt}. Therefore,

α⁡(t)=ℒ−1​{A⁡(s)}​(t)=α⁡(0)​[r2r2−r1​er1​t−r1r2−r1​er2​t].\alpha(t)=\mathcal{L}^{-1}\{A(s)\}(t)=\alpha(0)\left[\frac{r_{2}}{r_{2}-r_{1}}e^{r_{1}t}-\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}-r_{1}}e^{r_{2}t}\right].

Equivalently,

α⁡(t)=α⁡(0)​[A​er1​t+B​er2​t],A=r2r2−r1,B=−r1r2−r1,\alpha(t)=\alpha(0)\Bigl[Ae^{r_{1}t}+Be^{r_{2}t}\Bigr],\quad A=\frac{r_{2}}{r_{2}-r_{1}},B=-\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}-r_{1}}, (25)

where

r1,r2=log⁡(β)±[log⁡(β)]2−4​λ2.r_{1},r_{2}=\frac{\log(\beta)\pm\sqrt{\bigl[\log(\beta)\bigr]^{2}-4\lambda}}{2}.

Since β∈(0,1)\beta\in(0,1), set L=−log⁡(β)>0L=-\log(\beta)>0. By the first order approximation,

(log⁡β)2−4​λ=L2−4​λ=L−2​λL+𝒪⁡(λ2L)\sqrt{(\log\beta)^{2}-4\lambda}=\sqrt{L^{2}-4\lambda}=L-\frac{2\lambda}{L}+\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\lambda^{2}}{L}\right)

Hence

r1,r2=−L±(L−2​λL)2+𝒪⁡(λ2L).r_{1},r_{2}=\frac{-L\pm\bigl(L-\tfrac{2\lambda}{L}\bigr)}{2}+\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\lambda^{2}}{L}\right).

This gives:

r1=−λL+𝒪⁡(λ2L),r2=−L+λL+𝒪⁡(λ2L).r_{1}=-\frac{\lambda}{L}+\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\lambda^{2}}{L}\right),\quad r_{2}=-L+\frac{\lambda}{L}+\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\lambda^{2}}{L}\right).

Plugging r1,r2r_{1},r_{2} into Eq. (25):

α⁡(t)≤C​α​(0)​er1​t=C​α​(0)​exp⁡(−λL​t)\alpha(t)\leq C\alpha(0)e^{r_{1}t}=C\alpha(0)\exp\!\Bigl(-\tfrac{\lambda}{L}t\Bigr)

for some absolute constant C>1C>1. Plug in L=−log⁡(β)=log⁡β−1L=-\log(\beta)=\log\beta^{-1} to finish the proof.
